text:
ben: FYI seeing a weird spike in WS_CONNECTION_RESET events from the proxy during last night's canary. console shows a bunch of 'stalled' sessions that got closed and then immediately reconnected.
priya: ugh that explains the duplicate billing counts i saw in the dashboard this morning :grimacing:
ben: exact counts — about 120 resets over 30m for tenant 'acme-pay'. billing counter increments on disconnect path before we detect resume, so short resets look like two sessions.
michael: do we have a short-lived proxy pool eviction happening? might be pool->backend idle timeout + keepalive mismatch.
sara: proxy (edge) config currently: ```idle_timeout: 30s
pool_evict_after: 45s
ws_ping_interval: 0 # disabled at the moment
```
sara: edge is owned by infra team, but we rolled out a routing policy that pins some customers to the new pool last night. that might've triggered churn.
priya: console UX: our session-lifecycle chart aggregates opens/closes and shows normal churn spike, but there's no marker for 'proxy-evicted' vs 'client-initiated' so it's indistinguishable. ops team flagged as billing issue.
telemetry-bot: detected missing tag 'conn_close_reason' on 38% of close events between 02:10-02:45 UTC.
ops-oncall: we should add a tag early in the close flow to avoid double-counting — i.e., mark 'counted_for_billing' before emitting client reopen metric.
michael: we also need to decide whether to re-enable ws pings. quick fix: set `ws_ping_interval: 20s` on edge and extend `idle_timeout` to 2m. longer-term: ensure proxy-initiated-close emits `close_reason=proxy_evicted`.
ben: agree. short-term plan: (1) enable pings on edge in canary (flag: edge.ws.pings=true), (2) bump idle_timeout in canary to 120s, (3) add telemetry tag and backfill counts for impacted window.
sara: i'll coordinate the edge flag deploy. ops-oncall, can you schedule a brief alert suppression for billing counters while we change config? want to avoid noisy pager storms.
ops-oncall: can do, 30min suppression window, note in #oncall.
priya: UX follow-up: i'll add a 'close_reason' column to the session table and a quick filter in console so PMs can filter proxy vs client closes. will mock tomorrow.
michael: one more internal API debate — our disconnect handler currently reports `close_signal` before persistence. if persistence fails we still counted it. we should reverse order: persist then emit billing event, or emit with idempotency token. thoughts?
ben: prefer idempotency token. less brittle across partial failures. add `billing_event_id` derived from session_id + seq.
priya: ok will update event schema. add this to rollout checklist.
sara: deploying canary now to 5% with pings + idle_timeout change. i'll post progress. :rocket:
deploy-bot: deploy started for edge.ws.pings=true -> canary-5% (edge-pool-b) at 2026-03-20T07:18:30Z
telemetry-bot: will emit a new metric `conn_close_emitter_stage` after the schema update. set to track for 72h.
ben: thanks team. follow-ups: PRs for idempotency + telemetry tag, console filter mock, and a retro if we still see duplicates after changes.
priya: noted. i'll create the console PR and link to the incident thread.
sara: can we add a small dashboard tile that shows 'reconnect-after-reset' rate (reconnect within 10s of close)? would help catch regressions.
michael: good idea — i'll add a prometheus rule: `rate(reconnects[1m]) / rate(closes[1m])` with label `reason=proxy_evicted` once we have the tag.
ben: Cool. closing loop: if anything weird on canary ping me directly. :eyes:
